title: Reaction rate - 123 school
heading: Reaction rate
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.q: What is the reaction rate?
questions.a: How fast the reactants disappear and the new substances are formed: how much substance reacts per second (or minute)

questions.q: What is the reaction time?
questions.a: How long the reaction takes, from the start until one reactant is used up

questions.q: A reaction goes faster. What happens to the reaction time?
questions.a: The reaction time becomes shorter: a faster reaction finishes sooner

questions.q: What happens to the reaction rate if you raise the temperature?
questions.a: The reaction rate increases: at a higher temperature the substance reacts faster

questions.q: What happens to the reaction rate if you lower the temperature?
questions.a: The reaction rate decreases: at a lower temperature the reaction goes more slowly, but does not stop at once

questions.q: What happens to the reaction rate if you increase the concentration of a reactant?
questions.a: The reaction rate increases: more particles per litre, so more collisions

questions.q: You make a solid finer, for example powder instead of a lump (greater degree of division). What happens to the reaction rate?
questions.a: The reaction rate increases: a powder has a larger surface area than a lump

questions.q: In a reaction between gases you increase the pressure. What happens to the reaction rate?
questions.a: The reaction rate increases: the gas particles are closer together (pressure only has an effect on gases)

questions.q: What does a catalyst do?
questions.a: A catalyst speeds up the reaction and is not used up at the end

questions.q: You raise the temperature. What happens to the reaction time?
questions.a: The reaction time becomes shorter

questions.q: You add a catalyst. What happens to the reaction time?
questions.a: The reaction time becomes shorter: with a catalyst the reaction goes faster

questions.q: You increase the concentration of a reactant. What happens to the reaction time?
questions.a: The reaction time becomes shorter

questions.q: Does the type of substance affect the reaction rate?
questions.a: Yes, some substances naturally react faster than others (sodium reacts much faster with water than iron does)

questions.q: Which of these things affects the reaction rate?
questions.a: The temperature (also: concentration, degree of division, catalyst, pressure for gases and the type of substance)

questions.q: You see a graph of the amount of reactant against time. The line slopes steeply downwards. What does that mean?
questions.a: The reaction is fast: the reactant disappears in a short time

questions.q: Name three factors that affect the reaction rate.
questions.a: For example: temperature, concentration, degree of division, catalyst, pressure (for gases) and the type of substance

questions.q: An effervescent tablet dissolves faster in warm water than in cold water. Which factor is responsible?
questions.a: The temperature

questions.q: Why does a powder react faster than a lump of the same substance?
questions.a: A powder has a much larger surface area, so more particles can react at the same time

questions.q: Small wood shavings catch fire faster than a large log. Which factor is responsible?
questions.a: The degree of division

questions.q: Why do you store food in the fridge?
questions.a: At a low temperature the spoilage reactions are slower

questions.q: Why is flour dust dangerous in a flour mill?
questions.a: The dust has an enormous degree of division (a very large surface area). It then reacts so fast with oxygen that it explodes

questions.q: A wood splinter burns much faster in pure oxygen than in air. Which factor is responsible?
questions.a: The concentration of oxygen is higher: air contains only about 21% oxygen, pure oxygen 100%

questions.q: A catalytic converter in a car makes sure that poisonous carbon monoxide is converted quickly. Which factor is used here?
questions.a: A catalyst

questions.q: You add a catalyst. How much product is formed in the end?
questions.a: The same amount as without a catalyst. The reaction is just finished sooner

questions.q: What is an enzyme?
questions.a: A catalyst in living organisms

questions.q: You let 5.0 g of zinc react with an excess of hydrochloric acid, first at 20 °C and then at 40 °C. What is different at 40 °C?
questions.a: The reaction is finished sooner, the same amount of hydrogen is formed

questions.q: Magnesium reacts with 2 mol/L hydrochloric acid and with 0.5 mol/L hydrochloric acid. In which solution does the reaction go fastest?
questions.a: In the hydrochloric acid of 2 mol/L: a higher concentration gives a higher reaction rate

questions.q: In a reaction 60 mL of gas is formed in 30 seconds. What is the average reaction rate?
Which two ways are useful for measuring the reaction rate when a gas is formed?
questions.a: Measure the gas volume per time, or measure the decrease in mass per time

questions.q: Why does the reaction rate usually become smaller over time?
questions.a: The reactants are being used up, so the concentration becomes smaller

questions.q: In a graph of the amount of product against time, the line becomes horizontal after a while. What does that mean?
questions.a: The reaction has finished, a reactant is used up

questions.q: You measure the reaction twice with the same amount of reactant. Line B rises more steeply than line A. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The reaction of B is faster, but B ends at the same height as A

questions.q: Name two ways to make a reaction go more slowly.
questions.a: For example: lower the temperature, make the concentration smaller, use a coarser (lumpy) piece or leave out the catalyst

questions.q: What is the reaction equation of magnesium with hydrochloric acid?
questions.a: Mg (s) + 2 HCl (aq) → MgCl<sub>2</sub> (aq) + H<sub>2</sub> (g)

questions.q: You measure the reaction rate of magnesium with hydrochloric acid. Which substance do you use for that?
questions.a: Hydrogen (H<sub>2</sub>), because you can measure the gas volume
